_about: How-to for each feature, shown on the Help page in the web app and the mobile app. Edit the text here; add a clip by filling videoUrl (a YouTube or other https link). Each step may also take an image (an https link to a screenshot).

sections.title: Getting started
sections.summary: Get your transactions in once, and Automonie keeps up from there.

steps.text: Tell us which banks and apps you use. We show the easiest way to connect each one.
Set up your first bank. For most banks that means forwarding alert emails; for app banks like OPay or Moniepoint on Android, it means letting us read the bank app's notifications.
Upload a recent statement if you want your history too. Nothing is saved until you review it.
Check Home for the banks still to connect.

sections.title: Forward bank alerts from Gmail
sections.summary: A one-time rule in Gmail sends every bank alert email to your private Automonie address. Do this on a computer, or in your phone's browser with Desktop site turned on: the Gmail app doesn't have these settings.

steps.text: In Automonie, open Accounts & alerts, then Email alerts, and copy your forwarding address.
Open gmail.com, click the gear (top right), then See all settings.
Open the Forwarding and POP/IMAP tab and click Add a forwarding address. Paste your Automonie address, click Next, then Proceed.
Gmail sends a confirmation. Its code and a Confirm button appear in Automonie by themselves within a minute; tap Confirm.
Back in Gmail settings, open Filters and Blocked Addresses and click Create a new filter.
In From, type your bank's alert address (for GTBank, alerts@gtbank.com; check a recent alert for yours). Click Create filter.
Tick Forward it to, choose your Automonie address, and click Create filter. From now on, every alert from that bank is forwarded.
Repeat the filter for each bank. Automonie shows Receiving once the first alert arrives.

sections.title: Forward bank alerts from Outlook
sections.summary: Outlook.com, Hotmail and Live accounts use a rule. Do this on outlook.com in a browser.

steps.text: In Automonie, open Accounts & alerts, then Email alerts, and copy your forwarding address.
Open outlook.com, click the gear (top right), then Mail, then Rules.
Click Add new rule and name it, for example Bank alerts.
Under Add a condition, choose From and type your bank's alert address.
Under Add an action, choose Redirect to and paste your Automonie address. If you don't see Redirect to, use Forward to.
Click Save. Automonie shows Receiving once the first alert arrives.

If Outlook says forwarding is blocked, your account may be too new for automatic forwarding; use a statement or notifications for now, or ask your bank to send alerts to your Automonie address directly.

sections.title: Read bank app notifications (Android)
sections.summary: For app banks like OPay, PalmPay, Moniepoint and Kuda: payments are logged as the bank app notifies you, with nothing to forward.

steps.text: Open Accounts & alerts, then Auto-capture, and read what's shared and what isn't.
Tap Allow notification access and switch Automonie on in the Android settings that open.
Choose which bank apps to read. Notifications from any other app are ignored on your phone and never sent to us.
If Android says the setting is restricted, open the app's info screen, tap the three dots and Allow restricted settings, then try again.

sections.title: Share an alert to Automonie
sections.summary: Got a bank text, a notification or a receipt? Share it to Automonie and confirm it.

steps.text: Long-press the alert text (or open the receipt) and tap Share.
Choose Automonie. We read the amount, date and who it was with.
Check it and tap Confirm. You go straight back to the app you came from.
If you already have that transaction, we tell you, so it isn't counted twice.

sections.title: Upload a bank statement
sections.summary: Good for bringing in history, or for any bank.

steps.text: Download a statement from your bank app or internet banking as PDF, Excel or CSV.
In Automonie, tap Import and choose the file. If it's password-protected, enter the password; we use it only to open the file and never keep it.
Review what we found. Nothing is saved until you tap Save.
We check the totals against the balances printed on the statement and tell you if anything doesn't add up.

sections.title: The Action Center
sections.summary: Anything we weren't sure about waits here for a quick decision, so your numbers stay right.

steps.text: Check transactions we couldn't read clearly: confirm, fix or remove each one.
Settle possible duplicates: remove the copy, or keep both if both are real.
Name subscriptions and accounts, and tell us which bank an unknown sender is.
Removed something by mistake? Tap Undo in the next five seconds.

sections.title: Accounts
sections.summary: Each bank account we spot, and any you add yourself.

steps.text: Name an account so you can tell them apart, and set its type.
Add an account we haven't seen with Add account. With the last four digits, its alerts land on it automatically.
If the same account shows up twice, use Merge.
Delete an account and choose whether to keep its transactions.

sections.title: Budgets
sections.summary: Set a monthly amount per category and see how much is left.

steps.text: Open Grow and add a budget for a category, or let us suggest one from your spending.
The bar turns amber near the limit and red when you're over.
We nudge you when a budget is nearly used up, if budget notifications are on.

sections.title: Goals
sections.summary: Track progress towards something you're saving for. Automonie never moves money; you record what you put aside.

steps.text: Add a goal with a target and a date.
Record money as you put it aside, wherever you keep it.
We celebrate at 25, 50, 75 and 100%.

sections.title: Subscriptions and bills
sections.summary: See what renews when, and get reminded before it does. Automonie never pays anything for you.

steps.text: We spot recurring charges like Netflix or DStv from your transactions. Track the ones that are real; tap Not one for the rest.
Add a bill with its due day to get a reminder three days before.
Want to cancel a subscription? Open it for the steps for that service, and we'll watch for the charge to stop.

sections.title: People
sections.summary: Who you send money to and receive it from.

steps.text: Tap the person on any transfer to say who they are: family, friend, business or you.
Their transfers, past and future, are sorted to match.
Filter your transactions by person, and see who you send to most in Insights.

sections.title: Notifications
sections.summary: At most two a day, never between 10pm and 7am, and no amounts on your lock screen unless you turn them on.

steps.text: Open Settings, then Notifications, to switch each kind on or off.
Show amounts in notifications is off by default.

sections.title: Your data and privacy
sections.summary: What we keep, and how to take it with you or delete it.

steps.text: We store only the last few digits of an account number, never your bank login.
Export your data from Settings at any time.
Delete your account from Settings; your data is deleted with it.
Read the full privacy policy at automonie.com/privacy.
